doc.title: James Moody — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Other bands at the Big Top: Dizzy and Benny Carter
summary: Gillespie's big band impressed him most, plus a Benny Carter band with J.J. at a Greensboro barn.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: When you were talking about the Big Top, did you get to see a lot of different groups that came through as a part of that as well as Dizzy's band?

No, the group that I saw most of all was like Dizzy. That was the one that -- that really impressed me that came there. The other band that I saw was Benny Carter [phonetic sp.] and Mack [indiscernible], and J.J. was with that band. And they played just out in the city in Greensboro and it was a white-wash -- a white-washed barn or something. But that, boy, when I first heard "Malibu" and -- and some of the songs, you know, they was a good band. Porter killed, but all those guys in the band. So the Big Top was -- I remember that mainly because of Dizzy. That band.
And you had already heard Dizzy's recordings, so you were -­
Well, only heard the small group, but this was the big band.
You know. Sonny Williams [phonetic sp.]? Sonny's dead. I don't know. I forgot, but it sounded good, man, I know we -- we were real excited to hear it. Yeah.
